briefs.body: Settle which health scale ships, using the operator facts: zero health means an instant explosion, crashes do no damage, and armour is identical in both modes. Read Working/Translation/T10_DAMAGE.md sections 1 and 7, Research/JC3Grab/DAMAGE_MODEL.md, Research/BatmobileGrab/DAMAGE_RULES.md and run Tools/scripts/damage_predict.py. For each of three routes (max_health 36000 as shipped, max_health 1200 with scaled channel armour, max_health 1200 with member damage multipliers) compute hits-to-kill for the nine BmAK arms and the three vehicle archetypes, and the ratio to BmAK's 24 heavy cannon hits of 50 against 1200. Pick the route whose ratios match BmAK within rounding and name every member path it writes; if none matches, name the closest and the exact remaining gap as a capability card. Write Tools/scripts/health_scale_ruling.py (--write, --check), Working/Damage/health_scale_ruling.md and the report. Label each figure decoded, derived or UNKNOWN. Do not edit T10_DAMAGE.md; the ruling is a new file that brief 9171 can cite. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Locate the BmAK death sequence in the files already decoded. Inputs: Research/BatmobileGrab/DAMAGE_RULES.md (14 damage entry points), NATIVE_TRIAGE.md section 4 (the four RVisualDamageComponent exports), PARTICLES_FEATURES.md, AUDIO_FEATURES.md, and the report death-explosion-carriers.md from brief 7953. Trace the bytecode of the TakeDamage branch that fires when health reaches zero with Tools/scripts/bmak_damage.py and upk_read.py: what it spawns (explosion archetype, particle system, DeathExplosionSoundArray entry chosen), any delay constant, and the call that kills occupants (script call or native stub). Also read the four RVisualDamageComponent exports and say whether they produce any intermediate visible stage. Write Tools/scripts/bmak_death.py (--write, --check), Research/BatmobileGrab/DEATH_SEQUENCE.md and .json. Every line carries package, export and offset, or the word UNKNOWN with what was tried and which native function would settle it. The exe consumer of occupant death stays UNKNOWN unless an instruction address proves it. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Find the Batmobile regeneration rate without running BmAK. The member HealthRecoverRate is a TArray<float> at +8220 in the vehicle class, one entry per difficulty (Research/BatmobileGrab/DAMAGE_RULES.md section 5). Read tmp/freebuff/reports/regen-reader-function.md, bmak-gog-live-batmobile-reader.md and bmak-live-values-to-rows.md first, then look for the value in three static places: the class default properties of the Batmobile archetype in the cooked packages, any archetype or ini override, and the save or profile structures that LoadHealth reads. Use Tools/scripts/upk_read.py for the default-property scan and say which difficulty index applies to the player's game (UNKNOWN if the files do not state it). Output Tools/scripts/bmak_regen_value.py (--write, --check), Research/BatmobileGrab/REGEN_VALUE.md and .json with every candidate value, its offset and its units (per second or per XP award; the earlier note says per award). If nothing is found, write the exact live read as one 5-minute step for the hook telemetry of brief 7982. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Pick the JC3 carrier for out-of-combat regeneration. Operator facts: health refills over time when the car is not under attack, and is full on every re-summon. JC3 has no regen member in the 52-type damage vocabulary (Research/JC3Grab/DAMAGE_MECHANISMS.md), so apply the closest-system rule: name the nearest members (a repair or heal property on CDamageable, an entity-script heal, the hook module drafted in brief 7986) with member paths and values, then state the gap. Use the trigger and delay that d03 and the report regen-reader-function.md decoded; where they are UNKNOWN, define the rate and the out-of-combat delay as named parameters with a default and the live check that sets them, never as invented lore. Write Working/Damage/regen_carrier.md and Working/Damage/regen_spec.json (parameters, trigger, off switch, log lines the telemetry of brief 7982 can show). The report must say which behaviour belongs in data and which needs the hook, and the one supervised test that proves it. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

BmAK shows no intermediate visible damage, while the build still carries donor smoke and burn thresholds (1050 and 250) and 24 Land_* part damage types on 59 parts. Audit every row that can produce a visible stage: the smoke and burn thresholds, OnPartReachedDamageState uses (Research/JC3Grab/USAGES.md), the part damage types in Working/Damage/bm_health.json, mesh-swap parts, and the effects T-FX22 and T-FX23. For each, give the member path, the current value in Builds/bm-RC4, the value that suppresses the stage until the zero-health explosion, and the evidence it is the nearest member. Check against Tools/scripts/bm_health.py so no value breaks the explosion route. Produce Tools/scripts/damage_stage_rows.py (--write, --check), Working/Damage/stage_removal_rows.json (row id, path, old, new) and a report; the RC5 damage build reads that json. Where no member can suppress a stage, write the capability card with the missing capability named. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Operator fact: crashes never damage, scratch or dent the Batmobile. Prove that every JC3 channel which could hurt a car is covered. List from Research/JC3Grab/DAMAGE_MECHANISMS.md and the vehicle_damage fields: impact (wall and vehicle), fall, fire, explosion splash, train, water, crush by script, mission kill zone, and the speed-based impact damage factor. For each channel say the member, the shipped value in Builds/bm-RC4, whether it hurts a car at all, and the value that makes the Batmobile immune except for the weapon hits that should kill it. Note which channels the hook (briefs 7982, 7986) would need because no data member exists. Also read tmp/freebuff/reports/collision-impact-effects-plan.md for deformation and sparks that must go with the damage. Output Tools/scripts/no_crash_audit.py (--write, --check), Working/Damage/no_crash_channels.md and .json, and the report. Mark any behaviour not shown by a file as UNKNOWN with the probe that decides it. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Two plans use impact_damage_factor in opposite directions: T-DM8 sets it to 0 as incoming collision damage to the Batmobile, while the traffic plan raises it to 2.25 as damage dealt. Read Research/JC3Grab/DAMAGE_MODEL.md around lines 43-50, tmp/freebuff/reports/traffic-ai-claims-audit.md, tdm7-contact-damage-speed-band.md, carrier-ram-and-dodge.md and Working/Translation/T_ROWS.jsonl rows T-DM7 and T-DM8. Decide, from member names and values in the fleet, which side the factor acts on, which other member carries damage the Batmobile deals to others (rotor_collision.damage_to_other_per_second and neighbours), and what each takes for the lore ram (kills on speed, strafe 2.25, boost 2.0, Research/BatmobileGrab/DAMAGE_RULES.md section 3.3.1). Output Tools/scripts/ram_direction.py (--write, --check), Working/Damage/ram_direction.md and a table of rows with old value, new value, evidence. Anything the files cannot settle is UNKNOWN plus the in-game number to read. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Define which JC3 attackers count as heavy against the Batmobile and what each does to it. Use Research/JC3Grab/DAMAGE_MODEL.md, the weapon tables from G2-11 in Research/JC3Grab, and the BmAK relationship that rifle and machine-gun fire leaves the health bar still while tank shells, missiles, mines and helicopter rockets reduce it (a player claim, to be confirmed in play). List each JC3 attacker class (infantry rifle, MG, shotgun, sniper, helicopter MG, helicopter rocket, tank cannon, RPG, mine, grenade, AA gun) with its damage type and channel, and search the weapon writers for any that writes the bullet_heavy channel. With the ruling of d01, compute hits-to-kill per attacker on the final tree with Tools/scripts/damage_predict.py --root, and list the attackers that should do zero. Output Tools/scripts/attacker_set.py (--write, --check), Working/Damage/attacker_table.md and .json, and the report. Mark every BmAK-side claim about which weapons hurt as UNKNOWN until the damage test confirms it. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Close the immunity rows. Wheels: front_wheels_damage and rear_wheels_damage skew_health is 400 at its ceiling, labelled not proven unbreakable. Small arms: option A (the invulnerable int32 at epe+1167) is unproven on the vehicle root, option B uses channel armour. From Working/Translation/T10_DAMAGE.md sections 1, 2 and 7, Research/JC3Grab/DAMAGE_MECHANISMS.md and the attacker table of d08, decide which option carries each immunity on the RC5 tree, with member paths, old and new values and the hits-to-kill it implies. If tyres can still burst, find the nearest member that stops it (tyre health, puncture speed, wheel detach), or write a capability card for the hook. Output Tools/scripts/immunity_rows.py (--write, --check), Working/Damage/immunity_rows.json and a report with a prediction for each row that the damage test cards will read. Do not edit the damage tree. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Operator fact: health is full on every re-summon. BmAK persists health (LoadHealth) and has a RebelDropTimer 1800 of unknown unit (Research/BatmobileGrab/DAMAGE_RULES.md section 4); JC3 Rebel Drop re-delivers a fresh car. Establish, from Research/JC3Grab/REBELDROP.md, the item record rows and the entity spawn data, whether a re-delivered car starts at max_health, whether the previous entity is removed on re-summon, and whether a cooldown exists in the item record or elsewhere. Compare with the regen spec of d04 so a destroyed car and a damaged car both come back full. State what a save and load does to the car. Write Working/Damage/resummon_health.md and a row list, plus Tools/scripts/resummon_health.py (--write, --check). Anything about runtime state not visible in files is UNKNOWN, with a pilot-card step written as a single observation that settles it. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Design and stage the hook module for the one gap data may not close: zero health must produce an immediate violent explosion and kill the occupants. Use the vehicle readout offsets from brief 7982 (health, max health, occupant list) and the scaffold of 7981 under Tools/hook/. Drawing on DEATH_SEQUENCE.md from d02 and the carrier report death-explosion-carriers.md, implement an isolated module with an off switch: detect health at or below zero once, trigger the donor explosion event and the BmAK death effect slot, apply lethal damage to every occupant, and mark the car destroyed so it cannot be driven. Log each trigger as JSON lines in the telemetry file. Every offset cites its source line or is marked to-confirm-live with its 5-minute check. No writes unless the module switch is on, and nothing touches the game folder. Stage Builds/hook-0008-death/ with a receipt and a --check that rebuilds the source hash. Report the offsets table and unresolved items. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Specify how the BmAK health bar (top left, shown in battle mode, element UC_SetHealth in Research/BatmobileGrab/HUD.md and HUD_SPEC.json) gets its value in JC3. JC3's HUD has no entity-to-HUD caller (STATUS.md, HUD bridge). Read the hook overlay design in tmp/freebuff/reports/hook-batmobile-hud-overlay.md and the telemetry fields of hook-live-vehicle-readout.md, then write the feed contract: the health fraction source, update rate, behaviour at 0 and during regen, hidden or shown per mode, and the exact overlay element fields. Include how the fraction is derived when max_health is not 1200 (see the d01 ruling). Produce Working/Damage/health_bar_feed.json and .md and Tools/scripts/health_bar_feed.py (--write, --check), which validates the json against the HUD_SPEC.json element names. The HUD lane builds the overlay; this brief hands it the contract and names the pilot-card observation (bar fraction after a known number of shell hits). Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Checkpoint over the ten damage desk reports (health scale, death sequence, regen value and carrier, stage removal, no-crash channels, ram direction, attacker table, immunity rows, re-summon). Re-read each report and run its --check. List every place where a later report changes a number an earlier one used (for example the d01 ruling against the d08 hits-to-kill table), and every UNKNOWN that two reports disagree on. Then open the queue files tmp/freebuff/queue/9171-rc5-health-explosion-no-crash.txt, 9123-rc5-air-control-and-ram.txt and 9124-rc5-flip-water-remote.txt, provided their reports do not exist yet, and edit them in place so their text cites the new files (health_scale_ruling.md, stage_removal_rows.json, no_crash_channels.json, ram_direction.md, immunity_rows.json, regen_spec.json) instead of the stale 36000 and smoke/burn text. Append a line starting Updated by review at the end of each edited brief naming what changed. If a queue file already has a report, leave it and write a fix brief request in your report. Output: the report and a table of edits made. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Offline read-back of Builds/bm-RC5-damage after brief 9171. Run Tools/scripts/rc5_damage.py --check, then recompute from the built bytes, with Tools/scripts/damage_predict.py --root, the hits-to-kill of the nine BmAK arms on the three vehicle archetypes and compare them with Working/Damage/health_scale_ruling.md and attacker_table.json. Confirm four absences by reading the built entity and module rows: no smoke or burn threshold below zero-health, no part damage type that detaches or swaps a mesh, impact_damage_factor 0 (incoming), and deform_scale 0. Confirm the explosion route rows exist and the occupant kill is either present or listed as a hook item pointing at Builds/hook-0008-death. Compare the branch record under Working/RC5/branches/ with the files on disk (counts and sha256). Write Tools/scripts/verify_rc5_damage.py (--write, --check), Builds/bm-RC5-damage/verify/readback.md and the report. Every mismatch becomes a row with owner and a proposed fix; no tree is edited. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Remove the contradictions the roadmap map found in the damage records, without editing the original files. Targets: Working/Translation/T10_DAMAGE.md says T-DM7 is out while T_ROWS.jsonl has it next; STATUS.md reads T-14 as 28 rows, 26 queued although those are the lamp rows T-L8 to T-L35; the health scale in T-DM1 against the d01 ruling; ArmourModeDamageReduction 0 against the operator fact that armour is identical in both modes. Using the reports of 7951 and d01 and d07, write Working/Damage/ledger_reconcile.md with one row per contradiction (record, line, current text, correct text, evidence) and Working/Damage/ledger_rows_v2.jsonl holding replacement rows in the T_ROWS.jsonl schema for T-DM1, T-DM7 and T-DM9. Add Tools/scripts/damage_ledger_check.py (--write, --check) which fails if a replacement row does not parse or disagrees with the ruling. The operator or the status lane merges the rows; you do not. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Write the damage pilot cards in the format of Working/Q/PILOT/CARD_FORMAT.md, new files named DMG_*.md in Working/Q/PILOT/. Required cards: DMG_SHOTS (count rounds from a pistol, rifle and MG until the bar moves, expected zero), DMG_HEAVY (count tank shells or RPG hits to destruction, expected from Working/Damage/attacker_table.json), DMG_EXPLODE (observe the explosion at zero health, whether occupants die, whether the wreck is undrivable), DMG_RAM (wall hit at 40 and 80 km/h, expected no damage and no mark), DMG_REGEN (damage, wait out of combat, read the bar), DMG_RESUMMON (destroy, re-summon via SPAWN_BATMOBILE.md, read the bar full). Each step uses only commands from the three source files that CARD_FORMAT.md names, reads state from the hook telemetry of brief 7982 where possible and from a frame otherwise, and writes a pass band taken from the prediction files, never a number invented here. Include the trap ids the cards defend against. Add a --check script Tools/scripts/dmg_cards_check.py that confirms the card shape and that every cited command exists in the source files. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Supervised in-game test, run only after the operator writes tmp/freebuff/APPROVED_Q.txt. Use cards LAUNCH.md, SPAWN_BATMOBILE.md, DMG_SHOTS.md, DMG_HEAVY.md and KILL.md from Working/Q/PILOT. Observation: the number of pistol rounds (up to 200), rifle and MG rounds, then tank-shell or RPG hits needed to destroy the car, in pursuit and in battle mode. Pass rule: small arms leave the health fraction unchanged within 0.01, and the heavy hit count equals the prediction in Working/Damage/attacker_table.json within one hit, identical in both modes (operator fact: armour is the same in both modes). Record telemetry lines and screenshots under Working/Q/results/damage-hits/ and a table in the report: attacker, count, predicted, delta. Decide the hypothesis H0, H1 or H2 from DAMAGE_MODEL.md and state which the numbers support. On fail, write a fix card in the GRAB_BACKLOG.md section 0.4 format inside the report, changing one value only, and name it for the damage fix-loop brief. Stop on any crash; run KILL.md. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Supervised in-game test after the operator's approval file exists. Cards: LAUNCH.md, SPAWN_BATMOBILE.md, ENTER_EXIT.md, DMG_EXPLODE.md, RECORD.md, KILL.md. Observation: with the player inside, destroy the car with heavy hits and record a 10 second clip around the last hit. Pass rule, all three: no smoke, burn or sparks before the last hit; the explosion begins within 1 second of the health fraction reaching zero in the telemetry; the player (and any passenger) dies; the wreck cannot be driven or re-entered. Then, from outside, repeat once with the car empty and note whether the explosion is the same. Save the clip, telemetry and frames under Working/Q/results/damage-explosion/ and tabulate observed against expected. If the occupant kill is missing, the fix card names the hook switch of Builds/hook-0008-death; if smoke appears, the fix card names the row in stage_removal_rows.json. One value per fix card. Use KILL.md at the end, even after a crash. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Supervised in-game test after APPROVED_Q.txt exists. Cards: LAUNCH.md, SPAWN_BATMOBILE.md, ENTER_EXIT.md, CONTROLS.md, DMG_RAM.md, SCREENSHOT.md, KILL.md. Drive into a solid wall at 40 km/h and at 80 km/h, into a parked civilian car, off a roof or ledge of about 20 m, and through a billboard or fence. Observation: health fraction from the telemetry before and after each, and one screenshot of the front end each time. Pass rule: the health fraction changes by no more than 0.001, no dent, scratch, smoke or panel deformation shows, and the other car is damaged or launched as the d07 ram table predicts. Operator fact: crashes never damage the Batmobile. A train or fire check goes in only if a safe spot is named in the card. Results under Working/Q/results/no-crash/. On fail, the fix card quotes the channel from Working/Damage/no_crash_channels.md and changes one value. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Supervised in-game test after APPROVED_Q.txt exists, using the regen module from brief 7986 (isolated switch on for this test only, switch state in the report). Cards: LAUNCH.md, SPAWN_BATMOBILE.md, DMG_REGEN.md, DMG_RESUMMON.md, SCREENSHOT.md, KILL.md. Step A: take the health fraction to about 0.5 with heavy hits, stay out of combat, and sample the telemetry each 5 seconds for 120 seconds; record the delay before regeneration starts and the rate. Step B: damage to 0.5 again, leave and re-summon with SPAWN_BATMOBILE.md, read the fraction. Step C: destroy the car and re-summon; read the fraction. Pass rule: the fraction rises monotonically out of combat after a delay and reaches 1.0 on both re-summons. The measured delay and rate are written into Working/Damage/regen_spec.json as live values, not judged against any lore number. On fail, one fix card per observation. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Supervised in-game test after APPROVED_Q.txt exists. Cards: LAUNCH.md, SPAWN_BATMOBILE.md, CONTROLS.md, SCREENSHOT.md, KILL.md plus DMG_HEAVY.md. Step A: raise heat to five stars with the console route of CONSOLE_RECEIPT.md, drive for 120 seconds under pursuit by cars and helicopters without leaving the car, and sample the health fraction every 10 seconds. Step B: stand a tank 50 m away, take 5 shell hits, and compare the fraction with the prediction in attacker_table.json. Pass rule: A, the car is alive after 120 seconds unless helicopter rockets or tank shells hit it; the drop per attacker matches the table within 10 percent. Record the attackers seen, using the telemetry. Results under Working/Q/results/heat/. On fail, name the attacker whose number is wrong and write a fix card changing that one attacker's channel value. This test is separate from the hit-count test of d17 because it uses real AI fire. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Turn the damage test reports into one corrected build plan. Read the five reports of the in-game damage tests (hit counts, explosion and passengers, no-crash, regen and re-summon, heat survival) and the fix cards they wrote. For each failed observation decide the single value to change, in order, one per original failure; refuse to bundle two changes. Re-run Tools/scripts/damage_predict.py with the proposed value to show the new prediction, and write the patch into Working/Damage/fix_round1.json (row, path, old, new, source observation). Do not edit a built tree: write the instructions for the damage re-build brief (rc5_damage.py, a new --round 2 option) in the report. If all observations passed, say so and write the closing line for the QX checklist. State in the report which values are now live-measured rather than derived. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Supervised in-game retest, only after APPROVED_Q.txt exists and the rebuilt damage tree of the fix round is installed by the operator. Read Working/Damage/fix_round1.json and run only the cards whose observation failed before (a subset of DMG_SHOTS, DMG_HEAVY, DMG_EXPLODE, DMG_RAM, DMG_REGEN, DMG_RESUMMON), plus LAUNCH.md, SPAWN_BATMOBILE.md and KILL.md. Pass rule: each retested observation falls in the band that its original failure report stated. One extra fix round per original failure is the limit; a second failure is recorded as a named blocker with the telemetry and clip, and not retried. Results under Working/Q/results/damage-round2/. Final table: observation, round 1, round 2, verdict, so the QX checklist can mark the damage rows closed or open. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

The game proved that a brand-new entity path never spawns, so the shipped Batmobile replaces the vanilla leaf v0300_car_kensington_sportsmuscle_debug (hash 1621485476, Builds/bm-RC4/receipt.json), not the dead _batmobile leaf 443190071. Rewrite every world row on that fact. Read Working/Translation/T15_WORLD.md, T_ROWS.jsonl rows T-WLD1 to T-WLD7, MODLOG.md near line 19682-19690, Research/JC3Grab/STANDALONE.md and the triage in tmp/freebuff/reports/l0-probe-triage.md. For each row give the old text, the corrected text (leaf, hash, category now military UIFlag 7, caption), and the evidence; add the backlog D-6 and B-13 lines in corrected form. Produce Working/World/rebased_rows.md, Working/World/rebased_rows.jsonl in the T_ROWS schema, and Tools/scripts/world_rebase_check.py (--write, --check) which fails if any row still names 443190071 as live. Never edit the originals. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Decide how the world behaviours that run on a condition (water teleport, flip recovery, regen) are carried. Question NEW-WLD-03: can JC3 execute mod-authored vehicle script or graph (.gsc, .gdc) from the dropzone, or must the native hook carry them? Search Research/JC3Grab and E:/Modding/JustCause3/_grab for any graph writer or loader precedent (file types, loaders in RTTI, mod examples), then compare with the hook design in tmp/freebuff/reports/native-hook-design-jc3mp-contract.md and the water signal candidates from water-detection-static.md. Write a verdict table: behaviour, data-only route (with evidence or UNKNOWN), hook route, the one supervised check for each. Hooks are permitted; so the answer is the closest carrier plus what the build must still write. Output Tools/scripts/logic_carrier.py (--write, --check), Working/World/logic_carrier.md/.json, and a statement for the rewrite of the 9124 queue text if its data-only route is unsupported. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Operator ruling: Rebel Drop is the summon, so remote driving and the homing call (LB sends the car to the player) may be halted if the reason is written. Produce those records. For remote driving (static overlay from about 100 m, no movement past 150 m), homing, and the drive-in arrival through car_drive_to_point.btc, write one halt record each: the BmAK behaviour with its source file, the closest JC3 system (member paths or file names), the gap, the evidence for why the Rebel Drop route supersedes it, what would reopen the halt, and the hook sketch if reopened. Sources: tmp/freebuff/reports/remote-control-range-static-overlay-plan.md, remote-and-autonomous-drive-plan.md, summon-drive-in-closest-system.md, summon-and-unranked-weapon-plans-v2.md. State that the .btc body decode (NEW-WLD-01) is deferred because nothing built depends on it. Write Working/World/HALTS.md/.json and Tools/scripts/halts_check.py (--write, --check) that fails if a record lacks any of the six fields. Do not edit queue briefs; the review brief applies your result. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Decode the three files that decide how enemies and police treat a vehicle: settings/factions.bin, global/heat.blo and settings/heat.gadfc. Locate them through Research/JC3Grab/INDEX.jsonl and the extracted game data under E:/Modding/_shared/gamedata. Start from tmp/freebuff/reports/traffic-and-ai-reaction-to-batmobile-plan.md, its controls 4 and 5. Use the repo's existing binary readers (Tools/scripts/jc3adf.py and neighbours) and write a reader Tools/scripts/ai_reaction_decode.py (--write, --check, the check re-decodes and compares record counts and a checksum). Report the schema, the faction table, how a vehicle is classed (model, entity name, hash or archetype), which heat events involve vehicles, and whether any field would make AI ignore, flee from or target a particular vehicle hash. Output Research/JC3Grab/AI_REACTION.md and .json. Label decoded, derived, or UNKNOWN with the byte range tried; a guess about a field name is not a result. Shared rules: E:/Modding/JustCause3/JC3-Batmobile/tmp/freebuff/INSTRUCTIONS.md.

Operator fact: enemies cannot pull Rico out of the Batmobile. Extend that to the empty parked car: confirm no NPC can steal or enter it. From Working/Translation/T9_INTERACTION.md (six hijack objects dropped), the entity graph of Builds/bm-RC4-entity and Builds/bm-RC5-entity, and the w04 decode, list every object and member that allows an AI to enter, hijack, pull the driver out or target the car as a vehicle to take: seat and door interaction nodes, hijack nodes, driver-eject on damage, AI vehicle-claim flags.
